analogue: Gas-phase α-pinene OH oxidation forms pinonaldehyde through its peroxy-radical chemistry and subsequent oxidation or photolysis of hydroxy hydroperoxides.
citation: α-pinene photooxidation under controlled chemical conditions – Part 1: Gas-phase composition in low- and high-NOx environments
evidence: Gas-phase analyses detected pinonaldehyde in controlled α-pinene oxidation; further conversion of hydroperoxide intermediates contributed to the low-NOx total pinonaldehyde yield.
difference: The fitted G_A delay, V_A molecular mixture and yield are bulk parameters; effective formation rates in the mixed-O₃/OH Manchester runs were not measured.
